title: Reunion of Siblings
next_chapter_hook: In the depths of the time-space rift, where does that call truly originate? Is it fate's guidance, or another chess game laid out by the Heavenly Dao's eye?

text.content:
The night sky above the Holy Sect Forbidden Grounds held no stars; heavy dark clouds hung low over the border between Tianqing Sect and Holy Sect, like a black curtain that could never be lifted. Chen Ji stood before the time-space rift, fingertips pressed against that crack emanating a cold, eerie glow, sensing that familiar blood resonance that made his heart tighten.

She was inside.

Eight whole years.

He had thought he had long forgotten what the little girl with double buns, always trailing behind him calling 'gege', looked like. But when that feeling of blood connection surged up, countless memory fragments he had deliberately sealed away broke free like a tidal wave—his mother's dying testament, his father's retreating figure before his disappearance, and those small hands desperately reaching toward him through the flames.

The night wind stirred his Servant Disciple's gray robe. Chen Ji took a deep breath, suppressing the churning emotions in his heart. The Tianji Record Fragment faintly heated within his consciousness, yet gave no warning—this meant that what he was about to do would not encounter fatal danger within these three hours.

The Holy Sect's patrol disciples had just passed; the restriction runes at the forbidden grounds' entrance flickered dimly in the darkness. Chen Ji drew out a Demonic Path Mist Talisman given to him by Ye Qing, crushing it gently. Ebony mist wrapped around his form like a living creature, completely concealing his presence.

He turned sideways and silently slipped into the time-space rift.

Inside the rift was a chaotic grayish-white space where the flow of time became indistinct. With every step Chen Ji took, he could feel the blood resonance intensifying, as if an invisible thread was pulling him forward.

Then he saw her.

At the far end of the grayish-white space, on a simple stone platform, a young girl in plain white prison garb stood with her back to him. Her figure was much slimmer than in his memories; long black hair cascaded over her shoulders, the tips startlingly streaked with gray.

"Nian'er..."

Chen Ji's voice was hoarse, those two words echoing through the chaotic space with warmth he had never shown anyone in eight years.

dialogue.content:
The girl's form stiffened slightly, then slowly turned around.

That face was five parts familiar and five parts foreign from his memories. Her once-round cheeks were now sharply defined; her eyes held a composure far beyond her years. Her eyes remained that same pair of clear orbs, yet now resembled an ancient well of unknowable depth, reflecting something Chen Ji could not comprehend.

"Bro...brother?"

Her voice trembled slightly, then was forcibly suppressed, "Why are you here? This place is dangerous, leave quickly!"

text.content:
Chen Ji didn't move. His gaze locked onto the mark between Chen Nian's brows—where a faint gray line stretched, like a dried riverbed or cracks spreading across porcelain, slowly extending from her brow center toward both temples.

That was the sign of soul separating from flesh.

Knowledge from the Tianji Record Fragment exploded in his mind, each word like a searing brand, searing his heart with agony. Retribution of fate's power—when a person's soul bears weight it should not, it begins to separate from the flesh. Once the separation completes, the soul loses all anchor and dissolves into nothingness.

Chen Ji clenched his fists tightly, nails digging deep into his palms.

dialogue.content:
Chen Nian seemed to sense his gaze and unconsciously raised her hand to cover her brow center, but Chen Ji seized her wrist.

"Don't look." Her voice was平静得不像一个十六岁的少女, "I know what this is."

"You know?" Chen Ji's voice dropped极低, "You know and you still..."

"I know." Chen Nian raised her eyes, meeting his gaze directly, "Since I can remember, I've known that brother carries something terrifying. Every time you use that ability, it leaves marks on you, then you grow weaker and weaker."

Her eye sockets slightly reddened, yet she stubbornly refused to let tears fall, "So when those people captured me, I thought—if I could bear part of it for you, wouldn't gege suffer less?"

text.content:
Chen Ji felt his heart being gripped tightly by an invisible hand, pain making it almost impossible to breathe.

The Executor Contract.

That was the shackle the Tianji Record Fragment imposed on him—each time he altered a foreseen future, fate's trajectory would backlash onto him. And Chen Nian... she had actually used her own soul as a vessel,分担了一部分反噬.

"How long?" His voice was hoarse, "How long has this shackle been on you?"

Chen Nian was silent for a moment, then softly said: "Since the day I was brought to the Holy Sect."

Eight whole years.

Chen Ji closed his eyes, took a deep breath. When he opened them again, his eyes had turned cold and black. The debt the Holy Sect owed him just grew heavier.

dialogue.content:
Chen Nian seemed to sense his emotional change and suddenly gripped his hand tightly.

"Brother, listen to me." Her voice grew urgent, "Don't seek revenge on the Holy Sect, don't act rashly—I can hold on, really."

She forced a smile, one carrying a hint of cleverness Chen Ji had never seen before, "Besides... I've gotten stronger too. They thought I was just a vessel, but they didn't know I can also draw power from them."

Chen Ji looked down at her other hand—layered in a faint golden glow, the color of fate's power, yet denser than any he had ever seen.

"You..."

"Brother taught me, didn't he?" Chen Nian blinked, "Playing dumb to eat the tiger."

choice.prompt: Chen Nian's growth brought Chen Ji a flicker of relief, yet the crack between her brows and symptoms of soul separation were like a thorn piercing his heart. He had to make a choice—forcefully remove the shackle now, or accept the current situation and seek a better solution?

choices.description: Immediately attempt to use the Tianji Record's power to forcibly strip the shackle, even if this may worsen Chen Nian's soul trauma.
choices.visible_cost: Consume a large amount of Heavenly Fate (-15 points), may worsen Chen Nian's injuries
choices.visible_reward: Immediately remove part of the shackle, delay the soul separation process
choices.risk_hint: Extremely high risk, may cause backlash to spiral out of control

text.content:
Chen Ji didn't hesitate again. He raised his hand, pressing it to Chen Nian's brow center. The power of the Tianji Record Fragment surged forth like a tide. Golden light collided with the gray crack between Chen Nian's brows, emitting an irritating hum.

"Brother! Don't—" Chen Nian tried to struggle, but found her body immobilized by a gentle yet irresistible force.

She felt the shackle loosening. That heavy chain she had voluntarily borne for eight years was being stripped from her soul one link at a time. But at the same time, she could clearly sense—each link removed meant a gray line appearing between Chen Ji's brows.

He was taking his shackle back.

dialogue.content:
"Enough!" Chen Nian grabbed Chen Ji's wrist abruptly, eyes red-rimmed, "Brother, you're mad! Do you know what you're doing?"

Chen Ji lowered his gaze to her, a faint curve appearing at the corner of his mouth, "I'm doing what an older brother should do."

He withdrew his hand, forcibly halting the shackle's removal—not because he didn't want to continue, but because the Tianji Record Fragment had already warned: continue any further and Chen Nian's soul would completely shatter.

He took a step back, only removing one-third. But this one-third alone caused his originally full Heavenly Fate to plummet by fifteen points.

choices.description: Temporarily accept Chen Nian sharing the shackle's burden, do not forcibly intervene, first seek other solutions.
choices.visible_cost: Cannot immediately alleviate Chen Nian's suffering
choices.visible_reward: Maintain stable Heavenly Fate, buy time to find alternative solutions
choices.risk_hint: Chen Nian's injuries may continue to worsen

text.content:
Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcibly suppressing the churning emotions in his heart.

He knew Chen Nian was right. Forcefully removing the shackle would not only potentially harm her but also leave him weakened—and in Holy Sect territory, weakness meant death.

He slowly withdrew his hand, voice low: "...Fine. I won't touch it for now."

Chen Nian clearly relaxed, but saw Chen Ji raise his head. Those eyes' coldness made her heart skip—the look she had seen in countless nightmares, the expression brother wore when he had made some unshakeable determination.

"But I will find a way." Chen Ji said each word deliberately, "I will find a method to completely remove this thing. Until then—"

dialogue.content:
He reached out, gently brushing the gray crack between Chen Nian's brows, his touch as delicate as handling a precious, fragile treasure.

"I won't let you die."

Chen Nian's eyes finally reddened. She turned her face away, voice carrying a hint of choking: "Brother is still the same as before, almost dying yourself but still worrying about others..."

Chen Ji said nothing. He simply stood there quietly, letting his sister release emotions she had suppressed for eight years. The chaotic space was silent, only Chen Nian's muffled sobs echoing.

Eight years of separation, eight years of endurance, eight years of bearing it alone—at this moment, finally found an outlet.

choices.description: Ask Mo Xiansheng if there are other methods to remove the shackles without harming Chen Nian.
choices.visible_cost: Consumes time, may miss the best opportunity for intervention
choices.visible_reward: Obtain more information about the shackles and removal methods
choices.risk_hint: Mo Xiansheng may not reveal the full truth

text.content:
Chen Ji didn't rush to make a decision. He closed his eyes, his consciousness sinking into the Tianji Record Fragment.

Mo Xiansheng's elderly form materialized in the void, his clouded eyes gazing toward Chen Nian's direction, a complex expression flickering across his face.

"Her condition is more serious than I anticipated." Mo Xiansheng spoke slowly, "This shackle isn't ordinary fate backlash, but—a fragment of the Executor's Contract."

Chen Ji's heart tightened: "What does that mean?"

"It means to completely remove this shackle, brute force alone won't suffice." Mo Xiansheng's voice was low, "It requires someone else who also carries the Executor's Contract to voluntarily share the burden."

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji remained silent for a moment, then suddenly said: "Can Su Qingyao's shared destiny ability do it?"

Mo Xiansheng's form wavered slightly, as if hesitating whether to tell him. Finally, he sighed: "Theoretically, yes. But the prerequisite is—she must do it willingly."

"And," Mo Xiansheng's voice became grave, "once the fragment of the Executor's Contract transfers, the original host will completely lose the fate connection with the Executor. In other words—she will never be able to sense your existence again."

This meant Su Qingyao would be reduced to a complete outsider.

Chen Ji opened his eyes, looking at Chen Nian who was watching him anxiously, a complex light flickering in his eyes.

text.content:
Time in the chaotic space seemed to freeze, Chen Nian's emotions gradually calmed. She released Chen Ji's sleeve, rubbing her eyes hard, trying not to look so disheveled.

"Brother, there's one more thing I need to tell you." Her voice suddenly became solemn.

Chen Ji looked up and saw an expression on Chen Nian's face he had never seen before—it was fear, yet mixed with an irrepressible curiosity.

"During my imprisonment..." She paused,似乎在组织语言, "I heard a voice."

"Coming from the depths of the temporal rift."

dialogue.content:
Chen Nian's pupils slightly contracted, her voice extremely low: "That voice said—it has been waiting for someone. Someone capable of breaking the chess game."

She looked at Chen Ji, faint lights flickering in the depths of her eyes: "That voice also said... the Tianji Record is not unique. On the other side of the temporal rift, there are other 'Tianji Records,' other 'Chess Players.'"

"Brother, this world... may be much larger than we imagined."

Chen Ji's heart rate suddenly accelerated. The Tianji Record is not the only one? Other Tianji Records? Chess Players?

This information exploded in his mind like thunder, completely overturning his original understanding of the world.

text.content:
Mo Xiansheng's voice suddenly sounded in his mind, carrying a solemnity never seen before: "What she said is true."

Chen Ji's consciousness was pulled into the inner space of the Tianji Record. Mo Xiansheng's form floated unsteadily in the void, his clouded eyes filled with complex light.

"In ancient times, there were seven Chess Players." Mo Xiansheng spoke slowly, "Each presided over a volume of the Tianji Record, jointly maintaining the fate balance of this world."

"But later, a... catastrophe occurred. Six volumes of the Tianji Record were shattered in that catastrophe, scattered across the mortal world. Only the volume I protect, hidden within your bloodline, barely survived."

Chen Ji remained silent for a moment, then suddenly asked: "What about the seventh Chess Player?"

dialogue.content:
Mo Xiansheng's form suddenly froze.

Silence.

Endless silence.

When Mo Xiansheng spoke again, there was an emotion Chen Ji had never heard in his voice—fear.

"The seventh Chess Player... was the mastermind behind that catastrophe."

"His name is—Heavenly Eye."

Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. Heavenly Eye—the transcendent consciousness he had always thought was the ultimate villain—was actually the seventh Chess Player? Was it actually a... counterpart of the Tianji Record?

Mo Xiansheng's voice continued to come, each word like a heavy hammer: "It has not disappeared. It is merely... waiting. Waiting for the right moment."

"And now, that temporal rift is its only connection to this world."

choice.prompt: The truth about Heavenly Eye left Chen Ji momentarily shocked. As someone who plans before acting, he had to decide what to do next—risk exploring the temporal rift, or retreat first to plan carefully?

choices.text: Explore the depths of the temporal rift
choices.description: Venture deep into the temporal rift to see if more clues about Heavenly Eye can be found.
choices.visible_cost: May encounter unknown dangers, significant time consumption
choices.visible_reward: May obtain key intelligence, even discover methods to counter Heavenly Eye
choices.risk_hint: Heavenly Eye may be waiting in the depths of the rift

text.content:
Chen Ji made his decision.

He nodded to Chen Nian, signaling her to wait here, then turned and walked toward the depths of the temporal rift. Chaotic gray-white churned around him, like countless unhardened dreams.

The deeper he went, the clearer the call became. That was not Heavenly Eye's voice—Chen Ji was certain. If it were that existence, he would have sensed that suffocating pressure.

It was a completely different being.

Finally, at the end of the gray-white expanse, he saw a door.

dialogue.content:
It was a pitch-black door, about three zhang high and two zhang wide, its surface covered with dense符文. Chen Ji had never seen those symbols before, but strangely, he could understand their meaning.

"The fragment of the Seventh Cycle of Rebirth Door." Mo Xiansheng's voice rang in his mind, with a tremor, "How could it be here..."

Chen Ji reached out, his fingertips touching the door's surface. An icy, piercing sensation instantly spread through his entire body, followed by countless scenes flickering before his eyes like a passing parade—

He saw a continent devoured by flames.

He saw six blurry figures joining forces against a massive eyeball.

He saw countless fragments of the Tianji Record scattered in the void.

Then, all returned to darkness.

choices.description: Don't act rashly, exit the forbidden grounds first, return to the Tianqing Sect before making plans.
choices.visible_cost: Miss the opportunity to obtain intelligence at the first moment
choices.visible_reward: Maintain safety, preserve strength, convenient for future layout
choices.risk_hint: Heavenly Eye may use this time to make arrangements

text.content:
Chen Ji withdrew his hand.

As someone who had lurked in the Tianqing Sect Servants' Quarters for three years, he deeply understood a truth—the more critical the moment, the less one should act rashly. Behind that door might lie tremendous fortune, but more likely a carefully designed trap.

Rushing in without sufficient intelligence was not what a strategist would do.

He turned and walked back to Chen Nian's side. Looking at his sister's worried gaze, the corners of his mouth slightly lifted: "Don't worry, I was just scouting ahead."

Chen Nian relaxed slightly, but didn't release her tightly gripping hand: "Then we..."

"Let's go back first." Chen Ji said softly, "Some things need to be carefully planned."

dialogue.content: Chen Nian nodded, a flicker of relief passing through her eyes. She rose from the stone platform, her movements steadier than Chen Ji had imagined—eight years of imprisonment had clearly not completely crushed this girl who once only knew how to cry. "Brother." She suddenly spoke. Chen Ji turned back. Chen Nian's smile appeared especially gentle in the chaotic grayish-white light: "It's good to see you again." Simple six words, yet they caused Chen Ji's heart, hardened by countless conspiracies and intrigues, to soften for a moment. He reached out and ruffled the top of Chen Nian's head, just as he had done countless times eight years ago. "Let's go." His voice was soft, yet carried an unprecedented determination: "Brother will take you home."

text.content: The light of the time-space rift gradually faded behind them. Chen Ji held Chen Nian's hand, passing through the barrier of the forbidden land and returning to the wilderness at the border between Tianqing Sect and Holy Sect. The night remained pitch-black, the dark clouds still hung low, but Chen Ji felt the darkness before him was no longer so suffocating. He had found his sister. Although her situation remained dangerous, although the road ahead was still full of thorns, at least—he was no longer alone. Chen Nian leaned against his side, her steps somewhat unsteady. The symptoms of soul extraction had not worsened, but the accumulated exhaustion of eight years was spreading through her body. Chen Ji silently adjusted his pace, slowing down so she could keep up.

"Brother." Chen Nian's voice suddenly sounded, carrying a trace of drowsiness: "That voice I mentioned earlier... it's been calling to me." Chen Ji's footsteps paused slightly. "I feel like," Chen Nian turned her head, those clear eyes sparkling with a faint light in the darkness, "it's not calling me." "It's calling you." Chen Ji fell silent. He looked up at the dark horizon in the distance, and a guess slowly formed in his heart—between the time-space rift, the fragment of the wheel of reincarnation, and the call Chen Nian heard... was there some kind of hidden connection? Mo Xiansheng's voice echoed in his mind: "The chess game of destiny is far older than you can imagine." And he, perhaps, was standing at the very center of this massive chessboard.

Chen Ji took a deep breath, temporarily suppressing his scattered thoughts. Whatever awaited him ahead, he had to take one step at a time. The complete truth of the Tianji Record, the Holy Sect's conspiracy, the布局 of the Eyes of Heavenly Dao, and the secrets behind the time-space rift—all of these needed to be uncovered by him. But at this moment, he only wanted to focus on one thing. Bringing his sister back to Tianqing Sect. Letting her no longer be imprisoned, letting her breathe the air of freedom, letting her smile under the sunlight like an ordinary girl. Even if this meant becoming an enemy of the entire world, he would not retreat a single step. Because he had promised his mother. He would protect Chen Nian with his life. This was the only oath he, as an older brother, would never break.

dialogue.content: Chen Nian seemed to sense the weight in his words, and suddenly laughed softly. "Brother, you've changed." Chen Ji raised an eyebrow: "How have I changed?" "The old you would only hide behind me, crying." Chen Nian's voice carried a hint of teasing: "Now you've become someone who says 'become an enemy of the world.'" Chen Ji stared at her speechlessly. This girl, not seen for eight years, had learned to joke around. "But—" Chen Nian's smile gradually faded, becoming serious: "I prefer the current brother." "Because only such a brother can protect Nian'er."

text.content: The night wind brushed across the wilderness, carrying the distant, faint bell sounds from Tianqing Sect. Chen Ji knew that when he returned, countless matters awaited him—Ling Yuan's surveillance, Su Qingyao's investigation, Han Lie's restless scheming, and the Holy Sect's随时可能发起的进攻. But at this moment, he merely walked quietly, letting his sister's hand rest in his palm. That hand was much thinner than in his memories, its knuckles so defined they felt somewhat硌人. But its temperature was real, its touch was real. This was not a dream. He had truly found Chen Nian back. And this time, regardless of what price he had to pay, he would never let her disappear from his side again.

Just as the two were about to reach the border of Tianqing Sect, Chen Ji's footsteps suddenly halted. His gaze fell on a hill in the distance—on it, a figure in blue robes stood with hands behind their back, as if had been waiting for quite some time. Moonlight filtered through the gaps in the clouds, illuminating that icy-cold face. Su Qingyao. Her gaze pierced through the night, falling precisely on the unfamiliar girl beside Chen Ji, a complex light flickering in her eyes. Chen Ji's heart sank slightly. Why was she here? What made him even more uneasy was—had she seen Chen Nian?

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao descended slowly from the hill, each step carrying an indescribable pressure. Moonlight flowed over her blue robes, reflecting a face as cold as frost. "Chen Ji." Her voice was clear and cold, neither joy nor anger discernible: "You travel at night and yet don't bring me along. Do you not trust Su Qingyao?" Her gaze shifted from Chen Ji to Chen Nian, her eyes narrowing slightly: "Or is it that this girl is more trustworthy than Su Qingyao?" Chen Nian instinctively hid behind Chen Ji, whispering: "Brother, who is she?" Chen Ji's brow twitched slightly. Trouble had arrived.

choice.prompt: Su Qingyao's appearance made the situation delicate. She had clearly already noticed Chen Nian's presence. As someone skilled in scheming, Chen Ji had to decide how to handle this sudden situation—should he confess the truth or continue to hide it?

choices.description: Explain to Su Qingyao that Chen Nian is his sister and what she has endured over the years.
choices.visible_cost: Expose his weakness and lose the initiative in front of Su Qingyao
choices.visible_reward: May win Su Qingyao's trust and help, even trigger the shared destiny ability
choices.risk_hint: Su Qingyao may not be able to accept Chen Ji's deception

dialogue.content: Chen Ji was silent for a moment, then raised his head, looking directly into Su Qingyao's eyes. "She is Chen Nian." His voice was calm: "My biological sister." Su Qingyao's pupils contracted sharply. She clearly had not expected this answer. "She disappeared for eight years." Chen Ji continued, his tone carrying a trace of weariness that was not easily察觉: "Captured by the Holy Sect, used as some kind of... vessel." He reached out and gently pressed his hand on Chen Nian's brow center, revealing the gray crack to Su Qingyao. "This is the mark of karma's backlash. She used her own soul to bear part of the shackles of the enforcer's contract for me."

Su Qingyao fell silent. Her gaze lingered on the crack at Chen Nian's brow center for a long time, her emotions complex and impossible to penetrate. After a long while, she spoke softly: "So... your abnormalities over these years were all because of her." Chen Ji did not speak, but his silence itself was an answer. Su Qingyao suddenly smiled, that smile carrying a hint of bitterness: "Chen Ji ah Chen Ji, you really are..." She did not finish, merely deeply glancing at Chen Ji before turning to walk toward Tianqing Sect. "Come find me in the Inner Sect tomorrow." Her voice drifted on the wind: "There are some things we need to discuss properly."

flags_set: 苏青瑶已知晓陈念身份

choices.description: Hide Chen Nian's true identity from Su Qingyao, fabricating some reason to deflect.
choices.visible_cost: May deepen Su Qingyao's suspicion and damage mutual trust
choices.visible_reward: Protect Chen Nian's information from being leaked, maintaining the secrecy of the layout
choices.risk_hint: Su Qingyao is extremely intelligent; lies may be quickly seen through

dialogue.content: A perfectly fitting expression of bewilderment appeared on Chen Ji's face. "What is Senior Sister Su saying?" He scratched his head: "This is just a lost girl I encountered on the road. Seeing she was pitiful, I brought her along..." Su Qingyao's gaze cooled. "Chen Ji, do you take me for a fool?" Her voice suddenly rose: "The fate energy on this girl is so dense it's practically overflowing. Are you telling me she was picked up on the road?" She stepped forward, her gaze sharp as a blade: "And that crack on her brow center—that's a sign of soul extraction. How could an ordinary girl possibly have something like that?"

Chen Ji sighed inwardly, knowing something was amiss. Su Qingyao truly wasn't so easily fooled. Just as he was about to speak, Chen Nian suddenly stepped out from behind him, gazing directly into Su Qingyao's eyes. "Sister Su." Her voice was calm: "My name is Chen Nian. I am Chen Ji's biological sister." Chen Ji猛地 turned his head, only to see Chen Nian shaking her head gently at him. "Brother, I know you want to protect me." A faint smile curved her lips: "But some things don't need to be hidden forever." She turned to Su Qingyao, her gaze carrying a maturity beyond her years: "Sister Su, you should truly care about my brother, right? Then we have nothing to hide from you."

text.content: The night wind blew again, carrying away the stagnant air between the three. Chen Ji gazed at Chen Nian's back, a complex emotion rising in his heart. This girl, reunited for less than an hour, had already dared to make decisions on his behalf. But he was not angry. Because what Chen Nian said was right—some things truly don't need to be hidden forever. He looked at Su Qingyao, this woman who had been investigating him, suspecting him, yet extending a helping hand when he needed it most. At this moment, she was looking at Chen Nian with an inexplicable gaze, as if reassessing this seemingly delicate girl. Moonlight fell, stretching the three figures' shadows long across the ground. Chen Ji suddenly felt that perhaps, from now on, he wouldn't have to walk the road ahead alone.
